A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 28-page versions of the same study, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices. The shared framework and retained experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial methodological and empirical revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoT generation and annotation results, layer/head localization, spectral analyses, and controlled perturbation experiments across three models.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds HarmBench experiments, reasoning-length analysis, baseline/runtime comparisons, critical-head mitigation, and MATH500/GPQA evaluations.

M1.justification: The specified method changes substantially: B2 becomes a routing-coordinate centroid instead of cross-sample angular dispersion, and B3 becomes entropy effective rank instead of top-K energy concentration. Equation 1 reverses the layer-selection contrast. Section 6 additionally introduces fine-tuning only critical-head parameters while freezing the remaining model.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained GossipCop-based fake-news task, v4 evaluates broader harmful instructions through HarmBench and tests general reasoning on MATH500 and GPQA after mitigation. These introduce substantive task and domain coverage absent from v1.

E2.justification: v4 Table 8 introduces evaluated attention-based comparators attributed to Zhou et al. (2025) and faithfulness-based comparators attributed to Lanham et al. (2023), reporting safety correlation and runtime on News and HarmBench. v1 contains critical-versus-random-head controls but no corresponding comparison against these alternative diagnostic methods.

E3.justification: v4 expands evaluation from three to five models, adding Flan-UL2 and DeepSeek-R1-70B, and introduces 0–1500 versus 1500–2000-token comparisons, mitigation evaluations, and per-sample timing/safety-label correlation protocols. B2/B3 evaluation definitions change. Appendix A.2 also changes the stated Qwen family from Qwen2.5 to Qwen3; the PDFs do not establish whether the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine whether longer CoTs intensify unsafe spectral signatures (Table 6), computational cost versus diagnostic correlation (Table 8), and reasoning-performance losses after mitigation (Table 9). These substantially extend v1's window-selection, prompting/style, perturbation, and case-study analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain input-wise variance bands and the Pearson-correlation calculation. v4 does not introduce repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing; its new tables continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds localization, length-sensitivity, baseline/runtime, and mitigation results. Table 4 reports average mitigation gains of 67.1 percentage points on News and 55.0 on HarmBench; Table 9 reports average reasoning losses of 1.5 and 1.7 points. Existing percentage annotations also change, including 28% to 18% in Figure 1 and 20.2% to 18.2% in Figure 2. These corrections are distinct from the newly reported experiments.

T1.justification: The layer-contrast definition and two central spectral definitions change. Appendix F replaces the B2 projector-dispersion argument and B3 top-K SVD approximation theorem with centroid properties and entropy-effective-rank statements and bounds. The softmax Jacobian, B1 theory, and most general perturbation proofs remain.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims diagnosis and localization of unsafe fake-news reasoning, presenting targeted mitigation as a future direction. v4's conclusion additionally claims generalization to broader harmful instructions and demonstrated parameter-efficient mitigation that largely preserves reasoning ability. The original claim that final refusal does not guarantee safe CoT is retained.

C2.justification: v1 interprets safe routing through directional consistency and concentrated spectral energy; v4 Section 5.2 instead emphasizes smaller coordinate displacement and broader spectral participation. It adds explanations linking longer reasoning to accumulated routing risk and interprets mitigation and cross-task results. Layer-position consistency across styles is qualified, although some retained concentration language conflicts with the revised energy interpretation.

D1.justification: v4 adds model-architecture/alignment documentation, sampled-row and power-iteration computation details, and timing hardware specified as 8×RTX 3090. Anonymous code access is replaced by named GitHub and project-page links. Conversely, Algorithm 1 drops the explicit zero-error threshold and 10×100 verification-sample annotation. These are limited documentation changes, without a complete new reproduction protocol.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting HarmBench, additional models, attention/faithfulness baselines, and several contextual claims. Mirsky is removed alongside the old SVD approximation argument. The related-work section's monitoring taxonomy and mechanistic-interpretability positioning remain largely unchanged; publication-metadata updates do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: The main narrative organization is retained. v4 polishes grammar and terminology, revises author/front-matter information, repairs appendix references and the catalogue, and condenses annotation pseudocode and some explanatory passages. New scientific sections extend the structure, but the existing document is not comprehensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Seven new tables present generalization, mitigation, model coverage, reasoning-length, runtime, and reasoning-retention information. v4 also adjusts front matter and float placement, moves retained case-study figures, compacts Algorithm 1, and corrects Figure 20's panel labels. Most original plot designs and plotted traces are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important gaps in v1 through broader-task evaluation, diagnostic comparisons, mitigation, and reasoning-retention checks, while correcting the layer contrast and percentage inconsistencies. However, the central metric rewrite leaves conflicting explanations: Section 4.2 associates safety with concentrated energy, whereas Sections 4.3.3 and 5.2 associate it with broader spectral participation. Retained spectral plots receive new definitions without clarification of recomputation, and new mitigation results lack training and sampling details. These substantive gains and unresolved methodological inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
